candidate_universe_examined: Go Discord, Go Slack, #go-nuts IRC channel
Published books: 'The Go Programming Language' (Donovan & Kernighan), 'Go in Action' (Ketelsen, St. Martin, Kennedy)

Global conference circuit: GopherCon (US), GopherCon Europe, GopherCon Africa, GopherCon Singapore, GopherCon China, GopherCon Israel, GolangConf, GopherCamp, GoLab, Go Conference (Japan), TinyGo Conf

findings.books_podcasts_talks: Multiple widely-cited published books and an active weekly-format podcast (Go Time) plus a long-running historical talks/presentations archive (talks.golang.org, A Tour of Go, Getting Started with Go) demonstrate durable, non-ephemeral public learning material beyond forum posts.
findings.community_wiki_and_groups: The community-maintained Go Wiki catalogs user groups and meetups across many cities, a diversity-focused outreach group (GoBridge), an independent Discourse forum, a comprehensive conference list, and a companies-using-Go registry.
findings.conference_density: Go has one of the denser annual global conference circuits observed among mainstream languages in this batch: a US flagship (GopherCon, described by aggregators as the world's largest and longest-running Go-specific conference) plus regional editions in Europe, Africa, Singapore, China, and Israel, alongside independent events (GolangConf, GopherCamp, GoLab, Go Conference Japan, TinyGo Conf) tracked on the official community wiki.
findings.official_support_channels: Go's own help page enumerates a dedicated discussion forum, live Discord support, a Slack channel, and an IRC channel, plus an FAQ, in addition to release-announcement mailing lists, an official blog, and official Bluesky/Mastodon/Twitter accounts and a monitored subreddit.
findings.qa_platform_scale_context: Go questions sit within a Stack Overflow corpus with tens of millions of questions and answers platform-wide, and the 'go' tag has been an active, continuously-answered tag since the language's early years; this raw platform-scale figure is used only as contextual proxy evidence, not as a standalone score.
findings.third_party_aggregation: Independent forum-ranking sites and dev-resource pages independently converge on the same core set of active Go community venues (Golang Bridge forum, Stack Overflow 'go' tag, dev.to Go section, r/golang), indicating consistent, externally-observable community presence rather than only self-reported official channels.

Go.limitations: Raw counts such as subreddit subscriber totals, Stack Overflow tag question counts, and conference attendance figures were not independently re-verified against a live API in this pass beyond secondary aggregator pages (e.g., frontpagemetrics.com, subredditstats.com), and such popularity/traffic proxies are treated per methodology as supporting context only, not as a standalone score. No non-English localized-documentation coverage was independently examined beyond the Go Wiki's own pointer to a NonEnglish page.
Go.normalization_rationale: Go exhibits the full predeclared checklist of channel types (official docs/wiki, real-time chat across three protocols, structured Q&A at platform scale, active social/forum presence, durable books/podcasts, and a dense multi-continent annual conference circuit) with externally corroborated (not merely self-reported) evidence for each, placing it near the top of the 0-100 band; the score is not the maximum because some evidence (e.g., precise localized/non-English documentation depth) was not independently confirmed in this pass.
Go.retrieval_route: web_search (provider-brokered) against: (1) go.dev/help and go.dev/wiki (official channel index), (2) dave.cheney.net historical learning-resources page, (3) third-party forum aggregator forums.feedspot.com/golang_forums, (4) golang/wiki Conferences.md on GitHub, (5) GopherCon official site, (6) Wikipedia Stack Overflow article for platform-scale context.
Go.selection_rule: Language-neutral, predeclared checklist of public-knowledge channel types (official docs/wiki, live chat, structured Q&A, social/forum, books/podcasts, conferences) verified via the language's official help/docs page plus independent third-party forum/community aggregators and conference registries, using the same retrieval routes and examination depth applied to every language in this evaluation batch.
